slots.hypothesis: The intraday volume-timing centroid is a persistent stock attribute. Its level is unpriced (the 36 archive candidates that contain it average 0.002). The peripheries seen so far are all monotone pow_* wrappers, which leave the z-rank unchanged, so the core has never really been tested. Any alpha should sit in its deviations and conditioning. The 16 seeds all break rank equivalence, each with a different operator set, in three classes. (A) Deviation from the stock's own history: cross_zscore, cross_madz, cross_rank, and a short-minus-long EMA. (B) Nonlinear decile-bucket conditioning on LogFloatCap, turnover and frozen-quote frequency, which also tests whether the core is a proxy. (C) Interactions of abnormal late volume with net buy pressure, time-weighted intraday return, Gini concentration and market state. The mechanism tested is closing-auction institutional price pressure that later reverts.

The only structures in this batch that do not collapse are bounded, scale-free intraday-shape statistics. This slot spreads that class beyond volume timing. Each statistic appears as a 20-day mean (an attribute) and as a deviation from its own 20- or 60-day history (an event). The statistics are: minute Close-Volume and Ret-Volume correlation, mean return of the heaviest-volume minutes, signed-volume net buy pressure, share of up-minutes, volume Gini, time pinned at the day high or low, price-grid coarseness, time-weighted intraday return and trend smoothness, and minute-return skew. A bare day_centroid(Volume) is included as a sufficiency probe, because the E slot can never evaluate the bare core.
